items.rationale: A new session starts with a fresh context, so the detail must have been saved outside the model and put into this request by the program (or fetched by a tool). The other options assume the model or its window carries memory between visits by itself.

Call 1 sends 2,000 + 100 = 2,100. Call 2 sends 2,100 + 40 + 500 = 2,640. Call 3 sends 2,640 + 60 + 300 = 3,000. The total is 7,740. An answer of 3,000 counts only the last call's input; adding each new piece only once misses that the history is resent.

Fitting is not the same as being worthwhile: every token sent is paid for on each call, and accuracy and recall can fall as the context grows. Search can miss things (a), retrieval does not train the model (c), and a model needs no memorized manual to read one (d).

items.rationale: Full credit needs both the action (check the current, authoritative status) and the reason (the note may be stale, since the status can change). Only one of the two is partial. Refusing or accepting the booking on the strength of the saved note alone is wrong.

items.rationale: Full credit needs the risk (the chunk lacks context, such as which machine, so it may be wrongly applied) and a fix to the stored chunks (add the machine, manual or section, or a short explanation, to each one, or make chunks keep that heading). Only one of the two is partial.
